maria: Heads-up — change to the package exports map in the JS SDK is breaking a couple of onboarding sample apps when deployed to edge runtimes (Vercel Edge + Cloudflare). Getting ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED and TS can't find types. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

alex: same, saw a report from a customer. Can you paste a stack trace / package.json?

maria: pasted minimal repro below — simple import in a worker: 
```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const c = createClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY') });
await c.predict('hi');
```
stack: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './dist/index.js' is not defined by "exports"`
package.json (relevant):
```json
{"name":"redwood-inference","version":"1.2.0","exports":{"./dist/index.js":"./dist/index.cjs"},"main":"dist/index.cjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```

sam: aha — the exports map only has the CJS path and the edge runtime tries to load ESM path (or bundler resolves import->module). Edge runtimes are strict ESM, so when they try to resolve e.g. ./dist/index.mjs it falls back to the exports map and fails. Also TS/IDE can't resolve types if the mapping doesn't expose the package root correctly.

jun: additional wrinkle — some bundlers (Vercel) will try to import the package.json -> import condition then pick the "import" entry. If that's missing, they don't fall back to main the same way Node does. So exporting only the cjs file makes ESM consumers break.

alex: quick repro I ran: change exports to: 
```json
{"exports":{".":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}}}
```
and the edge runtime stopped throwing that path-not-exported error.

maria: thanks. But types still don't show up in TS playground / editors in the edge samples. I tried adding top-level "types":"dist/index.d.ts" and still nope for some users.

taylor: TS lookup logic is quirky when exports is present. If you have an exports map, TS will only resolve types if you either ensure the package root has a "types" field pointing at the .d.ts or you provide a separate export subpath for the typings. A pragmatic pattern we've used elsewhere: keep top-level "types" + add a types entry in the exports mapping: 
```json
{"exports":{".":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}},"types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
(not perfectly spec-pure but works for most tools)

sam: alternative: ship a small ESM entry that re-exports from the CJS bundle so old tooling keeps working. Also, include a subpath for the package.json if runtime tries to import package.json. Example: `"exports": { ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}, "./package.json": "./package.json" }`

maria: sounds like we should revert the export-map-only-cjs change for a patch release and then publish a follow-up that adds the import/require/types entries. Agree?

jun: +1 on revert. Also recommend we add a tiny CI job that runs the sample apps on a Vercel Edge emulator and Cloudflare pages preview to catch regressions.

alex: i'll open a release blocker PR to revert and include a changelog note. Also adding a docs warning about how export maps interact with edge runtimes and TS.

taylor: for short-term workaround for customers: ask them to import the specific file path (e.g., `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs'`) or pin SDK to previous patch. Not ideal but useful while we ship a fix.

maria: tracked as action items:
- alex: revert exports-only change -> patch release (high)
- sam/jun: add edge smoke tests to CI + sample-apps (medium)
- docs team: add guide on package exports + edge + TS (low)

dev-bot: Deploy started for revert branch (looks fine in staging) :rocket:

maria: thanks team. I'll follow up in PR and add the specific repro links to the issue. :thumbsup:
